subject: Follow-up: On-prem air-gapped deployment questions & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@legacybank.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Apr 30, 2027 at 3:12 PM -0700
Subject: Follow-up: On-prem air-gapped deployment questions & next steps

Tom - thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and the items we discussed that I wanted to capture and make actionable: 

- Primary ask: Legacy Bank is evaluating an on-prem, air-gapped deployment of Redwood Private for customer-facing document summarization.
- Key constraints: no outbound network, strict maintenance windows, quarterly offline patching, and existing rack-level procurement process.
- Questions we need to answer for your infra and procurement teams: recommended hardware SKUs (GPU type and node count), guidance on chassis/compatibility, on-site operational playbook (start/stop, upgrades when disconnected), and evidence for SOC2/audit log configuration.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Vivek to propose hardware baseline and offline upgrade workflow (attached: redwood_onprem_hardware_recs_v3.pdf).
2) Scheduling a 60-min deep dive with your infra lead to validate node counts and power/space requirements - can you share 2x windows next week?
3) We will provide a short runbook for air-gapped upgrades and an evidence checklist for your auditors.

I've attached our latest hardware recommendations (PDF) and will follow up with the runbook once Vivek confirms. If you prefer, we can loop in procurement in the next meeting so they can flag any PO timing or preferred vendors.

Thanks -
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@legacybank.com>

Date: Mon, May 03, 2027 at 09:08 AM -05:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: On-prem air-gapped deployment questions & next steps

Marissa - thanks for the summary and for capturing the action items. A few quick answers and clarifications: 

- We are indeed air-gapped for the environment that will handle PII. No outbound egress allowed; all updates must be delivered on USB or via a locked internal repository.
- Maintenance windows: primary window is Saturday 0200-0600 ET; secondary window can be Tuesday 2300-0200 ET (we prefer Saturday if possible).
- Procurement: I will introduce you to our procurement lead, Sara Moreno (cc'd). She will need an itemized SKU list and preferred vendor part numbers. We also have a preferred systems integrator (SI) for rack installation.

A couple of follow-up questions for your team: 
1) For offline upgrades, do you support an airgap bundle (signed tarball + checksums) or do we need to use a bespoke appliance you ship?
2) Any specific NIC/Fabric requirements? We run a mix of 25/100GbE and Mellanox switches.

Happy to set the deep dive for Saturday if you can make that window.

Thanks,
Tom Ellis
Dir. Infrastructure Engineering
Legacy Bank

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: On-prem air-gapped deployment questions & next steps

Tom / Marissa - looping in with the hardware and offline ops guidance. Short answers up front, happy to expand in the deep-dive: 

- Offline upgrades: we typically provide an airgap bundle (signed tarball + SHA256 checksums) that your infra team can transfer via secure media. We also offer an encrypted appliance image if you prefer a sealed image for provisioning. Both options require checksums and a short verification step in our runbook.
- Hardware baseline (starting point for 1000 QPS inference workload, batch=1, 512 context): 4 nodes with 8x H100 80GB (or 8x GH200 where available) per node for headroom; for smaller budgets 6x H100 per node is acceptable with slightly reduced throughput. We can tune further based on your latency SLOs.
- NIC/Fabric: 100GbE preferred for multi-GPU NVLink traffic, Mellanox is fully supported. No special switch features required beyond standard L2/L3 routing and jumbo frame support (MTU 9000 recommended).
- Maintenance process: our runbook supports an orchestrated offline upgrade - staged node-by-node with pre-checks and post-checks, and an option for a full cold-swap if you prefer minimal live changes. We'll include playbook templates for outage and rollback steps.

I've attached the hardware recommendations PDF to this thread (redwood_onprem_hardware_recs_v3.pdf) and will drop a draft of the airgap runbook by EOD PDT for review.

If Saturday 02:00-06:00 ET works for your team, let's pencil it and I can bring our infra lead. Otherwise propose alternatives.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com
